issues.description: Missing start.sh entrypoint script referenced by the exercise instructions and both Dockerfiles. The problem statement (Part 2, Dockerfile instructions) tells students to COPY a start.sh into the Docker image, make it executable, and use CMD ./start.sh. The template Dockerfile contains TODOs that instruct copying/making/executing start.sh, and the solution Dockerfile actively copies start.sh, sets permissions, and sets CMD to ./start.sh. However, neither the template nor the solution repository root contains a start.sh file in the provided repository listings. This missing file will cause the Docker build/deploy steps described in the exercise to fail and will block students from following the deployment instructions.
issues.suggestedFix: Provide the start.sh script at the repository root (and include it in the template) with the expected behavior (e.g., invoking java -jar /app/app.jar or delegating to the built jar) and ensure it is executable. Alternatively, if you prefer not to include a script, update the Dockerfiles and the problem statement to use a valid existing entrypoint (for example, replace CMD ./start.sh with CMD ["java","-jar","app.jar"]) and document the change. For educational clarity, add a short README or a comment showing the exact contents and required permissions for start.sh so students can reproduce the deployment steps reliably.
